source.branch: When theft makes an angry shopkeeper pursue the hero, stolen_value calls hot_pursuit. The helper calls rile_shk, copies the player name into customer, sets following, clears floor no_charge flags, and clears pet-carried no_charge flags before the monster turn.
callers: The following monster turn reaches muse.c:use_offensive after hot_pursuit changes the shopkeeper from peaceful to angry.

evidence: Fresh focused replay before correction: /tmp/A2-v52-minetown-muse-scan.json at commit 3b34371d46a47005b16613508fb9e4ce78e70b5a; the recording, manifest, recipe hashes match the admitted v52 input.

The immutable C screen at step 572 reads `The giant mimic vanishes!  Y-crad booms: "wizard, you are a thief!"--More--`; JS emits the same line without the marker. The mismatch is C `-` versus JS blank at row 0 column 67. A read-only recorder/source probe confirmed record-session uses stdin/stdout pipes without a PTY, sets TERM=xterm-256color, and falls back to termcap co#80. C topl.c:262-279 calls more() before appending a next message that cannot fit after the 67-character line with its eight-column margin.
Step 573 records Y-crad’s wand message. C muse.c:1877-1884 emits that message before the first rn2(8), so the C-only More is the expected wait before that next message.

C shk.c:stolen_value issues Norep, then calls hot_pursuit and angry_guards(FALSE). Norep defaults to MSGTYP_NOREP and does not itself force More; topline overflow before the next monster message causes the wait.

C shk.c:hot_pursuit calls rile_shk, copies svp.plname into customer, sets following, clears no_charge on fobj, and calls clear_no_charge_pets. JS shk.js:stolen_value now invokes the new hot_pursuit implementation at the matching source position. Existing JS helpers rile_shk, clear_no_charge, and clear_no_charge_pets implement the dependencies; clear_no_charge_pets was previously closed under port-shk-clear-no-charge-pets.

The implementation scope of delivery 20763e5c8c468f81294b4648414e6ed942b786b0 is shk.c:hot_pursuit and its active shk.c:stolen_value caller, reached from pickup.c:mbag_item_gone on this admitted path. Other hot_pursuit gaps at unrelated caller sites remain outside that task. The corrected exact replay matches through zero-based segment 0 step 583; its next C RNG site is monmove.c:m_move at step 584, with the source cause traced separately to shk.c:shk_move's avoid threshold.

After implementation commit c78575762, the exact admitted recording matches every screen, cursor, and RNG call through zero-based segment 0 step 583. The first later RNG mismatch is step 584 in the immutable recording / segment 1 step 585 in the fresh-recipe report: C rn2(20)=2 at monmove.c:m_move:1971 while JS emits rn2(5)=2. A disposable JS replay trace identifies that extra call at priest.c:move_special:612 -> shk.c:shk_move:3413. The trace's keeper is at (55,14), hero at (55,6), and JS has squared distance 64, hero.ushops nonempty, appr 0, and avoid false. C shk.c:shk_move uses distu(gtx,gty)>8; hack.h:1531 defines distu as dist2, so C sets avoid true at this distance. priest.c:move_special:83-87 then skips the (55,15) candidate marked NOTONL (0x00200000) in C, while JS admits it and makes one extra rn2(5) draw. The next C draw is rn2(20) in m_move. The first screen difference is at zero-based boundary 606. The matching prefix was verified by node scripts/synthetic-range-evidence.mjs .cache/task-evidence.json.

Focused checks pass: node --test scripts/shk.test.mjs; node --test scripts/shop-billing.test.mjs scripts/dokick-shipping.test.mjs; npm run lint. The latter two tests retain their source-gap assertions for distinct out-of-scope hot_pursuit call sites.
